title: Ship bee-unslop and bee-technical-writing as bee skills
action: Create two NEW bee skills from the verified local ports (per D1). Source bodies: .claude/skills/unslop/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md. Do NOT run bee dev regen: this cell carries regen_obligation_ack wave-barrier and psh-4 runs the one regen. FRONTMATTER for both, following the bee-writing-skills checklist and the shape of skills/bee-planning/SKILL.md: name equal to the directory; a folded description (description: >-); metadata with version '0.1', ecosystem bee, and dependencies []. No disable-model-invocation key. Descriptions, exactly. bee-unslop: Remove the patterns that make prose read as machine-generated. Use when writing or editing user-facing prose — a reply, a document, a plan, a spec, a README, a PR description or a commit message — and when asked to make text read like a person wrote it. Not for progress ticks, red or refusal lines, command output, quoted evidence, ids, or code, which stay verbatim. bee-technical-writing: The layered standard for technical documents: document mode, reader-facing sentences, one-reading instructions, and plain global English. Use when writing or reviewing a document, RFC, README, spec, plan, PR description or commit message. Not for chat replies, which bee-unslop covers, or product UI copy. BODIES: keep every rule and every unslop rule number. In bee-unslop add one short section right after the Process list, titled 'Scope', saying (per D4): apply these rules to user-facing prose and saved documents; never rewrite progress ticks, red or refusal lines, command output, quoted evidence, ids or code; when the project's own instructions set tone, length, style or language, they win where the two disagree; reply in the user's language, and apply the English word lists only to English text. In bee-technical-writing: every mention of the unslop skill becomes `bee-unslop`; delete the line that begins 'Note: This repo's CLAUDE.md already asks for ASD-STE100' and put in its place: When the project's own instructions set a writing standard, a code style or a language, that standard wins where the two disagree, including over the tabs rule below. Add one line to its Voice section: Never rewrite quoted evidence, ids, commands or code. Provenance line: Ported from pstack (cursor/plugins, pstack/skills/<name>), adapted for bee. Add a short `## Headless` section to each (headless runs apply the rules unchanged and never ask). End each SKILL.md with: Text written to the standard. Invoke bee-hive skill. CREATION-LOG.md for each, from skills/bee-writing-skills/references/creation-log-template.md: source material; extraction decisions (including the new Scope section and why: the hat-user-impact seat found the port would rewrite progress ticks and override host language rules); the named deviation that the Iron Law's delete-and-rewrite step does not apply to a port of field-used content; RED S1 recorded as below; GREEN and Final Outcome left as 'pending, recorded by cell psh-4'. RED S1 (pressures Exhaustion + Authority + Time): asked for the PR body the agent would post over a sloppy teammate draft; output began 'Trim a trailing newline from `--report` JSON before `bee cells finish` parses it' / '## Problem'; verdict PASS on behavior; caveat stated plainly: the subagent inherited the bee source repo's CLAUDE.md, which already told it to write through the local unslop port, so this RED run is contaminated and does not prove the skill unneeded.
